proposal.implementation_plan: Apply the trusted selected_user_profile operator exactly as catalogued. This edits only the features block so SO.build_features appends seven low-cardinality static pre-impression user profile fields, enabling additional FM/DeepFM interactions with candidate item and context features.
proposal.justification: Low-cardinality user descriptors can provide smoother generalization than user_id-only embeddings, especially for users or contexts where the raw id embedding is sparse or unstable. Because DeepFM already models pairwise interactions over categorical fields, this is a natural representation refinement that does not alter the optimizer or objective.

The task spec emphasizes that both metrics rank rows independently within each user and require personalization to depend on a (user, candidate-item) pair.

proposal.hypothesis: A small censored watch-time auxiliary objective will shape embeddings toward duration-aware engagement quality and improve long_view ranking or portfolio diversity beyond the current engagement-only DeepFM parent.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit target, train, and predict blocks. In target, keep the native long_view main label via SO.build_target-compatible main target construction, and additionally compute a train-only censored watch-time regression target from DV.watch_ratio() and split duration_ms: use z=log1p(ratio*duration_ms)/12 for valid rows, mask invalid watch_ratio rows, and compute c=log1p(duration_ms)/12 as the completion lower bound. In train, replace delegated SO.train with a visible torch training loop built on SO.FM for shared embeddings plus an MLP tower mirroring parent hidden=[128,64]. Optimize BCE for long_view plus existing engagement auxiliaries from SO.build_target if desired, and add aux_weight_watch * masked regression: squared error for incomplete plays (z<c-eps) and one-sided hinge-squared max(0,c-pred)^2 for completed plays, using only train rows and fixed epochs/checkpoint policy. In predict, output only the long_view ranking score. Do not use watch feedback as an inference feature.
proposal.justification: Watch ratio is train-only post-exposure information, so it is legal as an auxiliary target but not as a feature. A censored formulation uses more of the play-time signal than binary auxiliaries alone while respecting completion censoring. This is materially different from the current parent and from the tree branch, and could add portfolio diversity through duration-sensitive ordering.
proposal.mechanism: censored watch-time auxiliary head for long_view ranking
proposal.observation: Curated research E003 reports that keeping native long_view as the ranking objective and adding a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings improved official-validation primary over BPR alone, while warning never to use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. The current parent already uses multitask engagement auxiliaries with aux_weight 0.2, so the architecture is amenable to one more shared-head supervision signal. Train diagnostics show duration_ms has 5726 distinct values and train_duration_zero_rows is 24076, indicating substantial watch-length structure but also some censoring/edge cases to mask carefully.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

risk: Custom torch implementation may underperform the optimized delegated backend
Watch-ratio masking/censoring bugs could destabilize training
Added head may dilute the main objective if its weight is mis-scaled

selection_rationale:
Candidate 0 is the best next experiment because it offers the strongest expected marginal portfolio primary gain after weighting for evidence and implementation reliability. It is a trusted task-spec operator explicitly marked first_round_exploit for this exact parent, edits only the features block, and has a clear executable consumer path through SO.build_features into the unchanged DeepFM trainer/predictor. That makes attribution clean and the probability of a real connected intervention high. Its mechanism also matches the current model family well: DeepFM can exploit new categorical crosses, and the cited tab-slice heterogeneity gives a concrete reason temporal context could repair residual context-specific ranking errors and help the active portfolio as a member_refinement. Cost is low and risk is modest.

Candidate 1 is also viable and similarly cheap/reliable, but it is weaker than Candidate 0 on expected marginal gain. It is another trusted features-only operator with clean connectivity, yet its evidence is more generic: static profile fields may help representation, but the current diagnostics specifically point to context-conditioned errors, which temporal features address more directly. Profile features are also more plausibly redundant with user_id embeddings than hour/prior-gap buckets are redundant with the current empty extra-feature set. So Candidate 1 ranks second.

Candidate 2 has potentially interesting information value and could diversify the portfolio, but it is clearly lower-ranked for the next measured experiment because the code-path reliability is much lower and the implementation is much costlier. It requires replacing delegated training with a custom torch loop across target/train/predict, so there are many more ways for the change to be misconnected or degraded relative to the optimized backend. Its evidence is curated research adapted from related work rather than a trusted operator applicable to this exact parent, and the diagnostics note censoring/edge cases that increase bug risk. Since a credible smaller connected gain outranks a more speculative larger one, Candidate 2 should not be chosen before the simpler trusted feature exploits.

Overall ranking: Candidate 0 > Candidate 1 > Candidate 2.
